name: cmd-2-switches-to-the-second-space
description:
Also in the same run - both chords are space moves and the fixture has three spaces to move between.

WHAT THE REPORT WAS. Cmd+1..9 belonged to the favourite tiles. A tile slot with nothing in it makes ActivateFavoriteInSlot DECLINE, and the dispatcher then falls through to super, where Chromium's own select-tab-N activates a tab of the shared strip. The strip is shared across every space, so activating a tab that belongs elsewhere drags the window to that tab's space. One press, two meanings, and neither table said so - which is why the diagnosis had to come before the fix.

WHY THE VLOG LINES ARE THE MEASUREMENT. 'hotkey goToSpace2 fired' comes from the dispatcher's own per-outcome logging: a chord that reached the map and was declined names its reason instead, and one that never arrived leaves no line at all. Chromium's select-tab-2 leaves none of the three. So the pair of lines separates 'the Atrium action ran' from 'the space actually moved', which SelectSpace logs at both ends.

OPT+TAB IS THE SECOND HALF. The core has shipped opt+tab for nextSpace since the store was written and ParseCombo refused it on every launch, because it carries neither cmd nor ctrl. It is accepted now for a NAMED key only - a character chord like opt+a still stays with the page. Sending it here proves the relaxed rule survives real AppKit delivery and not just the parser, which a browsertest calling prePerformKeyEquivalent directly cannot show.

actions.note: ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

from the second space, Arc's cycle chord moves on to the third

assertions.label: the-digit-reached-the-space-action
assertions.desc: Cmd+2 ran goToSpace2. Chromium's select-tab-2 leaves no such line, and neither does a declined chord.

assertions.label: the-window-moved-to-the-second-space
assertions.desc: The rail actually moved. The line above says the action ran; this says it did something.

assertions.label: no-favourite-jump-behind-it
assertions.desc: One press, one action. The tiles hold cmd+opt+2 now, so nothing here should reach them.

assertions.label: no-tile-slot-resolved
assertions.desc: The other half of the old double meaning - the window never even looked up a tile for this digit.

assertions.label: opt-tab-reached-the-cycle-action
assertions.desc: the combo the map refused on every launch now binds AND arrives through real AppKit delivery.

assertions.label: opt-tab-cycled-forward
assertions.desc: Opt+Tab moved the window on from the second space to the third.
